chunks: 41—What al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from one who informed him, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“If the moon is eclipsed and the man wakes up but does not perform salat (prayer), then he must perform ghusl (ritual bath) the next day and make up the salat. But if he did not wake up and did not know of the eclipse of the moon, then nothing is upon him except making up the prayer, without ghusl.”

And al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: The ghusl of the newborn at the time of his birth is a sunnah (prophetic tradition). Its mention has already preceded in the hadith of ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā from Samāʿah.

key_terms.الْقَضَاءُ: make-up performance of a missed act of worship
key_terms.الْقَمَرُ: the moon, in the context of a lunar eclipse
key_terms.وَلْيَقْضِ: let him make up, meaning perform qaḍāʾ

ai.seo_question: What must a person do if he misses the salat of a lunar eclipse according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the eclipse prayer when the lunar eclipse is missed. It distinguishes between one who became aware and neglected the salat, for whom ghusl and qaḍāʾ are mentioned, and one who remained unaware, for whom only qaḍāʾ is required; it also notes that washing the newborn at birth is a sunnah (prophetic tradition).
